evidence.claim: IEA Electricity 2026 identifies AI, data centers, advanced manufacturing and broader electrification as important drivers of rising electricity demand.

IEA Energy and AI states that global data-center investment nearly doubled since 2022 and reached about half a trillion dollars in 2024; it also notes that building new transmission lines can take four to eight years in advanced economies and that wait times for critical components such as transformers and cables have doubled in the past three years.
evidence.source_title: IEA Energy and AI - Executive Summary

evidence.claim: NERC's 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment highlights rising resource-adequacy risks as electricity demand grows from data centers, industrialization, electrification and DER adoption.
DOE states that distribution transformer lead times increased from three to six months in 2019 to 12 to 30 months in 2023, driven by supply, labor and material constraints.
evidence.source_title: DOE Supply Chain and Market Analysis

evidence.claim: DOE reliability materials describe federal efforts to identify at-risk regions and guide interventions as the grid faces explosive load growth from AI and reindustrialization.
Eaton reported first-quarter 2026 record results, with 12-month rolling average order acceleration in Electrical Americas up 42%, driven by data-center momentum.
evidence.source_title: Eaton Reports Record First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Eaton's Q1 2026 analyst presentation reported total backlog growth of 44% in Electrical Americas and approximately 240% growth in Electrical Americas data-center orders.
evidence.source_title: Eaton First Quarter 2026 Earnings Release / Analyst Presentation

memory_update.text: PWR should remain a reference benchmark for grid execution and qualified electrical labor, not an underfollowed alpha candidate, until backlog, labor and margin evidence show a stronger chokepoint premium.

BWXT is a priority underfollowed nuclear-supply-chain hypothesis because generalists may classify it as defense/government nuclear exposure, but its commercial nuclear/SMR/materiality evidence must be verified before promotion.
CCJ is best used as a nuclear fuel-cycle reference leader and pricing benchmark rather than an underfollowed discovery name.
SMR should remain in the speculative_shadow lane because project financing, customer commitments, licensing, cost and construction timelines are the decisive survival tests.

VST, NRG, ETR, SO, NEE and BEPC are mostly power-asset or regulated/contracted generation mappings; they validate demand and power-market tightness but are less direct physical bottleneck suppliers than transformers, switchgear, construction labor or nuclear fuel/components.
FLNC remains an underfollowed storage/flexibility hypothesis, but margin quality, warranty risk, battery sourcing and backlog conversion are gating evidence items.

Need primary-source SEC filings and latest earnings materials for every ticker in this chunk; current company-specific evidence is sparse except for broader grid-demand context and Eaton electrical backlog references from cached Layer 2A evidence.
Need current market-cap, valuation, analyst coverage and price-performance checks to distinguish true underfollowed names from already-consensus AI power beneficiaries.
Need regional evidence for power-asset names: PJM/ERCOT/Southeast/Gulf Coast load growth, capacity-market outcomes, hedging, rate cases, IRPs and large-load contracts.
Need nuclear-specific evidence for BWXT, CCJ and SMR: DOE awards, NRC licensing, HALEU/fuel-cycle constraints, signed customer contracts, component qualification and project financing.

summary: Mapped the provided candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the Energy and Power Chain theme. The chunk is dominated by reference leaders in grid execution, nuclear fuel/generation, merchant/regulated power, renewables and storage. The strongest evidence-supported bottleneck in this chunk remains grid/electrical execution and transformer/switchgear-adjacent demand, but several tickers here are asset owners or speculative developers rather than physical chokepoint suppliers. Underfollowed candidates in this chunk should be treated as hypotheses until filings, backlog, contract, regional load-growth, regulatory and margin evidence are verified. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
